Predict mean plant weight

Source: R/kb_predict_mean_weight.R
kb_predict_mean_weight.Rd

Combine a weight and a size fit into the expected weight per plant of each site-year: wet or dry (kg), or carbon or nitrogen (g).

Usage

kb_predict_mean_weight(
  weight,
  size,
  new_data = NULL,
  wetdry = NULL,
  carbon = NULL,
  nitrogen = NULL,
  ...,
  measure = c("wet", "dry", "carbon", "nitrogen"),
  new_levels = c("sample", "average"),
  representative_site = NULL,
  n_plants = 100L,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3,
  progress = c("bar", "none"),
  progress_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

weight

A kb_fit_weight object.

size

A kb_fit_size object.

new_data

A data frame of the rows to predict at, with site and year columns (either may be absent, as in a grid from kb_new_data()), or NULL for the site-years in the size fit's data. year may be numeric or character: 2022 and "2022" match the same fitted year.

wetdry

A kb_fit_wetdry object, required for dry, carbon, and nitrogen biomass, or NULL. All fits must be of the same species and have the same number of draws.

carbon

A kb_fit_carbon object, required for carbon biomass, or NULL.

nitrogen

A kb_fit_nitrogen object, required for nitrogen biomass, or NULL.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

measure

A string, one of "wet" (kg), "dry" (kg), "carbon" (g C), or "nitrogen" (g N), giving the weight to predict.

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is shown for a site or year not in the fit. Sites and years in the fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "sample" (the default): a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

  • "average": the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

representative_site

A character vector of sites whose effects a new site takes in every fit (averaged when several are named), a list naming the sites per fit, such as list(weight = "site_a"), where a fit left out follows new_levels, or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

n_plants

A whole number of sizes averaged per draw to compute the mean plant weight; larger values are more precise and slower to compute.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

progress

A string, one of "bar" (the default, a console progress bar) or "none" (silent).

progress_dir

A string giving an existing directory in which to record progress for kb_progress(), or NULL (the default) to record none.

Value

A kb_predictions object: the rows of new_data with added weight_support and size_support, the draws of the mean weight in a weight_kg, dry_weight_kg, carbon_weight_g, or nitrogen_weight_g column, and estimate, lower, and upper.

Details

Mean plant weight is the weight model averaged over the site-year's size distribution (see Methods). weight_support and size_support show the data each fit has for the site-year, from most to least local: "site-year", "site, year" (its site and its year, but not together), "site", "year", or "none".

See also

kb_predict_biomass_in_situ() for the biomass of in situ surveys.

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_canopy(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), kb_predict_carbon(), kb_predict_cover_calibration(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_size(), kb_predict_weight(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_weight(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

set.seed(1)
kb_predict_mean_weight(fit_weight_sim_nereo, fit_size_sim_nereo)
#> <kb_predictions> response: weight_kg | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 45 × 8
#>    site      year  weight_support size_support    weight_kg estimate lower upper
#>    <fct>     <fct> <chr>          <chr>          <rvar[1d]>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 otter_co… 2020  site-year      site-year     0.86 ± 0.15    0.839 0.621  1.2 
#>  2 otter_co… 2021  site-year      site-year     0.85 ± 0.15    0.839 0.611  1.18
#>  3 otter_co… 2022  site-year      site-year     1.19 ± 0.22    1.17  0.84   1.68
#>  4 otter_co… 2023  site-year      site-year     0.92 ± 0.18    0.905 0.604  1.32
#>  5 otter_co… 2024  site-year      site-year     1.00 ± 0.18    0.98  0.692  1.4 
#>  6 otter_co… 2025  site-year      site-year     1.19 ± 0.21    1.17  0.846  1.65
#>  7 gull_rock 2021  site-year      site-year     0.89 ± 0.16    0.872 0.631  1.25
#>  8 gull_rock 2022  site-year      site-year     1.20 ± 0.21    1.17  0.846  1.67
#>  9 gull_rock 2023  site-year      site-year     1.52 ± 0.27    1.48  1.06   2.12
#> 10 gull_rock 2024  site-year      site-year     0.81 ± 0.14    0.796 0.566  1.1 
#> # ℹ 35 more rows

# The typical year at each site
kb_predict_mean_weight(
  fit_weight_sim_nereo,
  fit_size_sim_nereo,
  kb_new_data(fit_size_sim_nereo, by = "site"),
  new_levels = "average"
)
